taxonomy.note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Native from the lower Mississippi region through Texas; regional treatments emphasize Gulf/coastal prairie and wet alluvial habitats.

evidence: Kew/POWO confirms Texas as part of the native range.
Flora of North America and USGS treatments describe the species as a wet-alluvial, low-prairie, marsh-margin/Gulf Coastal Plain species.
NPSOT describes it as relatively rare in the wild and native to coastal prairies and marshes.
The user's iNaturalist tracker has one wild observation, but user observations are not converted into county-native proof.
target_zone_range.blocking_issue: No set of three exact project target-zone counties has been independently verified.
target_zone_range.guardrail: Do not infer target-zone native counties from garden use in Austin/San Antonio or from a single wild observation.

morphology.look_here_first: Start with scale and habitat. Gulf Coast penstemon has much smaller lavender-to-violet flowers, about 10–14 mm long, on slender branched stems in wet alluvial or coastal-prairie settings. The calyx lobes are small and sharply pointed, and the exserted staminode carries orange hairs distally.
diagnostic_traits: perennial herb with slender erect branched stems
opposite sessile oblong to lanceolate leaves
calyx lobes ovate to lanceolate, about 3.1–6 mm, sharp-tipped
corolla small, about 10–14 mm, lavender to violet
staminode exserted with orange hairs toward the distal half

confusers.separator: P. cobaea has enormous 35–55 mm pale flowers and broad serrate leaves on dry prairie/limestone sites.
P. triflorus has larger 25–35 mm pink/red flowers and a dry Edwards Plateau limestone ecology.
P. baccharifolius is a woody-based cliff subshrub with thick leathery leaves and red flowers.

installation_guardrail: Do not install as a project-native taxon until three exact target-zone counties are verified.
